questions.question: Mopin is the cultural festival of which Indian state?

__
 
• **Mopin** is primarily celebrated by the** Galo tribe** of **Arunachal Pradesh**, although other tribes in the region also participate in the festival.
 
• The festival is usually held in the **month of April **and is dedicated to the** goddess Mopin-Ane**, who is believed to **bless the harvest** and bring **prosperity** to the community.
 
• The festival is marked by various rituals and customs such as the **Mopin Oyi (offering) ceremony, the Popir dance,** and the traditional **Mopin feast.**
 
• The festival is an important occasion for the Galo community to come together, showcase their **cultural heritage, and strengthen social ties.**

• **Maharashtra **is a state in **western India** that is known for its **diverse culture, history, and cuisine**.
 
• Some of the popular festivals celebrated in Maharashtra include **Ganesh Chaturthi, Diwali, and Holi.**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India empowers the President of India to pardon in case of punishment or sentence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 72.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 72** of the Constitution of India empowers the President of India to **grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions** of punishment or to **suspend, remit or commute **the sentence of any person convicted of any offence.
 
• This power is vested in the President as the head of the** executive branch** of the government.
 
• The President can exercise this power in **consultation with the Council of Ministers**, but is not bound by their advice.
 
• The power of pardon is an important check on the** judiciary** and ensures that the punishment meted out by the courts is not excessive or unjust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 66:** The Vice-President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting at such election shall be by secret ballot.
 
• **Article 78** lays down a few duties and responsibilities for the Prime Minister as stated: To inform the President of all significant decisions made by the Council of Ministers regarding the management of Union affairs and other legislative proposals
 
• **According to Article 65** of the Constitution of India, Vice President can act as President or discharge his functions.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about nuclear fission.

options.text: The nucleus of a heavy atom, when bombarded with low-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.
Nuclear fission is the coming together of high-energy electrons and low-energy neutrons.
The nucleus of a low-energy atom, when bombarded with high-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.
The nucleus of a low-energy atom, when bombarded with high-energy neutrons, can be split apart into heavier nuclei.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The nucleus of a heavy atom, when bombarded with low-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nuclear fission** is a process in which the nucleus of a** heavy atom is split **into lighter nuclei.
 
• This process is usually initiated by **bombarding the heavy nucleus** with **low-energy neutrons.**
 
• The splitting of the nucleus releases a** large amount of energy** in the form of** heat and radiation,** which can be harnessed for practical purposes.
 
• Nuclear fission is used in **nuclear power plants** to generate electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear fusion** is coming together of **high-energy electrons** and **low-energy neutrons. **
 
• The nucleus of a low-energy atom is not heavy enough to **undergo fission.** 
 
• Only heavy nuclei, such as **uranium and plutonium**, are **capable of fission.**
 
• Nucleus of a low-energy atom cannot be **split apart into heavier nuclei.**
 
• Fission only produces** lighter nuclei.https://www.acs.org/careers/chemical-sciences/areas/organic-chemistry.html#:~:text=Organic%20chemistry%20is%20the%20study,phosphorus%2C%20silicon%2C%20sulfur).**

questions.question: When did the infamous Jallianwala Bagh incident take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13 April 1919.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **infamous Jallianwala Bagh** incident took place on **Sunday, April 13, 1919.**
 
• It was a** tragic incident **where British troops under the command of **General Reginald Dyer** fired upon a crowd of** unarmed Indian civilians** who had gathered for a peaceful protest against the arrest of two nationalist leaders.
 
• The incident resulted in the deaths of at least **379 people** and injured over a thousand others.
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre was a turning point in** India's struggle for independence** and led to widespread protests and outrage against British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Jallianwala Bagh is a **public garden l**ocated in** Amritsar, Punjab, India.**
 
• The incident is also known as the** Amritsar Massacre or the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.**
 
• General Dyer's actions were widely **condemned,** and he was eventually **relieved of his command** and forced to retire from the army.
 
• The incident led to the formation of the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, a major civil disobedience campaign led by Mahatma Gandhi, which played a significant role in India's struggle for independence.
 
• The Jallianwala Bagh site has been preserved as a** national monument **and serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made by the** Indian freedom fighters** in their struggle against British rule.

questions.question: Identify the Mauryan king who gave up conquest after winning a war.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka** was a **Mauryan king **who** gave up conquest** after winning a war.
 
• He was known for his policy of** non-violence** and promoting** peace and harmony.**
 
• Ashoka's change in attitude towards war and violence came after the** brutal Kalinga War**, which took place in **261 BCE.**
 
• The war resulted in the** death of thousands of people **and left Ashoka deeply remorseful.
 
• After the Kalinga War, Ashoka embraced **Buddhism **and promoted its teachings throughout his empire.
 
• He also implemented policies to promote **social welfare and religious tolerance.**
 
• Ashoka's reign is considered to be a** period of peace and prosperity **in ancient India.
 
• He is also known for his **rock edicts and pillar inscriptions,** which provide valuable insights into the social and political conditions of his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bindusara **was the son of** Chandragupta Maurya** and succeeded him as the Mauryan king.

 
 
• He continued his father's** policies of expansion and conquest **and is known for his conquest of Deccan.
 
 
 
• **Dashratha **was a king of** Ayodhya** and the father of **Lord Rama** in Hindu mythology.
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the **Mauryan Empire **and is known for his conquest of the Nanda Empire.
 
 
• He later renounced his throne and became a** Jain monk.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a source of protein?

• Different types of meat contain varying amounts of** fat and protein**. For example, **chicken breast** is a lean protein option, while **bacon** is high in fat and may not be the healthiest protein choice.
 
• **Milk** is a** source of protein **and is often consumed as a post-workout recovery drink due to its high protein content.
 
• Milk also contains **calcium**, which is important for **bone health and muscle function.**
 
• It can be consumed in various forms, such as **cow's milk, almond milk, or soy milk.**
